title: The income statement

match.reason: The bank has a general point on profit, but none teaches the income statement or how to calculate gross profit, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: The income statement
card: An income statement shows a business's revenue, expenses and profit or loss over a period of time, such as a month or a year.
Revenue is the income earned from selling goods or services. Expenses are the costs of running the business, such as wages, rent and advertising.
Gross profit = sales minus cost of goods sold. Cost of goods sold is what the business paid for the stock it sold.
Net profit = gross profit minus other expenses. If expenses are greater than gross profit, the business has a loss.
draft.remember: An income statement covers a period of time and ends in a profit or a loss.

a.q: An income statement shows which of these?
opts: Revenue and expenses over a period
Assets and liabilities on one date
Cash held by the business today
Money the owner plans to spend
a.why: An income statement reports revenue, expenses and the resulting profit or loss over a period. Assets and liabilities on one date belong to a different report, so that option is wrong, even though it is also a financial report.
a.clue: Think of a report that covers a month or a year.

b.q: Priya's shop in Orange sold $90 000 of goods that cost her $55 000 to buy. Her other expenses were $40 000. What does her income statement show?
opts: Gross profit of $35 000 and a net loss of $5 000
Gross profit of $50 000 and a net profit of $10 000
Gross profit of $35 000 and a net profit of $5 000
Gross profit of $90 000 and a net loss of $5 000
b.why: Gross profit = $90 000 - $55 000 = $35 000. Other expenses of $40 000 are greater than that, so the net result is a loss of $5 000. Taking only the $55 000 of costs from sales and ignoring the other expenses would wrongly suggest a profit.
b.clue: Take other expenses off gross profit, not off sales.

a.best: Revenue and expenses over a period

b.best: Gross profit of $35 000 and a net loss of $5 000
